title: A finite integral cover of a normal integral scheme has a sheaf norm
statement:
Let $p:Y	o Z$ be a finite surjective morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Suppose each local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. There are an integer $d\geq1$ and maps $
u_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ for all open $V\subseteq Z$, compatible with restriction and preserving multiplication and $1$, such that $
u_V(p^\sharp a)=a^d$ for every $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, and $b(y)=0$ implies $
u_V(b)(p(y))=0$ for every $b\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $y\in p^{-1}V$. Here values at points are taken in their residue fields [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case); the norm of positive degree is defined in Section 0BCX (divisors-section-norms), conditions (1) and (2).

proof.text: Apply the affine-field-data lemma to $p$. It gives $p(\eta_Y)=\eta_Z$, the single finite extension $\iota:L=k(Z)\hookrightarrow K=k(Y)$, and its positive degree $d$. On every nonempty affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, it gives a finite domain inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A=\Gamma(p^{-1}U,\mathcal O_Y)$ with $B$ integrally closed. Its generic-germ embeddings $\rho_U,\sigma_U$ realize $L,K$ as fraction fields and satisfy $\sigma_U(p^\sharp b)=\iota(\rho_U(b))$.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), affine rings and function fields

proof.text:
Apply the domain-norm lemma to each inclusion with these specified embeddings. Step 1 supplies its finiteness, normal-base and commuting-square hypotheses. Its unique maps $
u_U:A	o B$ preserve multiplication and $1$, satisfy $
u_U(p^\sharp b)=b^d$, and have generic formula $ho_U(
u_U(a))=N_{K/L}(\sigma_U(a))$. Thus every chart uses the single function $F=N_{K/L}:K	o L$ and the same positive integer $d$.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), affine restriction of the field norm

proof.text:
Use the affine-gluing lemma with this $F$, $d$ and the maps $
u_U$. Generic-point preservation comes from step 1; the generic and scalar formulas come from step 2. The lemma extends the affine maps uniquely to $
u_V$ on every open $V$, commuting with all restrictions, preserving multiplication and $1$, and satisfying $
u_V(p^\sharp b)=b^d$. Its unique map on the empty open also covers restrictions to that open.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), compatible affine maps and global norm, property (1)

proof.text: If $V=\varnothing$, there is no point $y\in p^{-1}V$, so the vanishing condition is vacuous. Otherwise fix such a point with $a(y)=0$. Choose a nonempty affine neighbourhood $U\subseteq V$ of $p(y)$. The affine-field-data lemma makes $p^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine vanishing criterion puts $a|_{p^{-1}U}$ in the prime $\mathfrak q$ corresponding to $y$. The domain-norm lemma puts its norm in $\mathfrak q\cap B$. Spectrum-map naturality identifies this contracted prime with $p(y)$, so the affine vanishing criterion gives $\nu_U(a|_{p^{-1}U})(p(y))=0$. Restriction compatibility from step 3 yields $\nu_V(a)(p(y))=0$. Evaluation of a section and its restriction at a point of the smaller open uses the same germ in the stalk and then the same residue-field quotient. Thus restricting to this affine neighbourhood preserves both the assumed zero value upstairs and the resulting zero value downstairs.
